parts.note: the parties are not festivities but the two people in a famous garden, the first couple in Eden

explanation.definitionFit: The biblical first man and woman were the two parties living in the Garden of Eden.

clue.text: The Spanish scholar brought up showing talent

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar

explanation.surface: A Spanish academic raised in a household that noticed early gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns ELBA (EL then BA) upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Being capable of doing something well is showing talent; a straightforward synonym.

definitions.meaning: to urge or speak in favour of something
in Scotland barristers are called ..., and senior ones take silk

explanation.walkthrough: A 'silk' is a senior barrister (King's Counsel), from the silk gown; in Scotland the equivalent lawyers are advocates.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means urges or supports; as a noun it is the Scottish title for courtroom lawyers.

clue.text: Troubled the French to get help outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for help goes round the French article

parts.note: aid means help
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A distressed French person needs outside assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailed is an old verb meaning bothered or afflicted, as in what ails you.

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of claimed are set out in another order

explanation.surface: A debater objects that someone has stated a point incorrectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' reorders CLAIMED.
explanation.definitionFit: A decimal point separates whole numbers from fractions, so the word is used alone for that dot.

clue.text: Transport Clive arranged to accommodate ambassador's return

indicators.note: to accommodate says one piece is housed inside the other
arranged says the letters of the name are put in a new order
return says the ambassador's letters go backwards

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is how an ambassador is addressed

explanation.surface: Clive organises transport so that a diplomat can get back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' makes VICLE from CLIVE; 'return' turns HE into EH, which goes inside after the V.
explanation.definitionFit: A car, bus or lorry is a means of transport, the general term for such conveyances.

clue.text: Back gas ring — it's needed for this pudding

indicators.note: Back says the word gas is read backwards

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Cooking instruction: the rear burner of the cooker must be used for this dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns GAS into SAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A milk pudding made from palm starch granules is a classic school dessert.

clue.text: In any case there's no trouble

indicators.note: the word any serves as a case or casing holding the other word

explanation.surface: A reassuring phrase: whatever happens, there will be no difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In any case' tells you to put NO inside ANY, after AN.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate or bother someone is to cause them trouble; trouble here is a verb.

clue.text: Went too far round and toppled

definitions.meaning: turned over-much, as if turned past the point of rotation

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the answer literally: over (too far) plus turned (went round).
explanation.definitionFit: Something capsized or upset has been turned upside down, tipped over.

definitions.note: the clue's noun stands for the adjective describing a kind of well, so the question mark flags a definition by example

indicators.note: developed says the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A plot of land is said to have been left unbuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' reworks the letters of AREA ISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bore drilled where pressure pushes groundwater up unaided is named after Artois, so this kind of well.

indicators.note: a palindrome reads the same in both directions, which this answer does

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to use a word that reads the same backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Disinclined is read literally as not inclined, without a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat surface has no incline, so dis-inclined in the literal sense means even.

indicators.note: secures says the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: to con is to study or learn
present as in here, in attendance
CE, Church of England

explanation.surface: A study confirms that the current church is in accord.
explanation.definitionFit: Logical consistency, where parts fit together in accord, is a kind of agreement.

definitions.meaning: a university teacher, given with a question mark as one example

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means purely theoretical; as a noun it is a university scholar such as a professor.

clue.text: The state of the Sphinx and the Pyramids!

definitions.text: The state of the Sphinx and the Pyramids!

parts.words: The state of the Sphinx and the Pyramids!
parts.note: state means a country, the nation where the Giza monuments stand

explanation.walkthrough: 'The state of' looks like asking about condition or repair; it means nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sphinx and the Great Pyramids stand at Giza, beside Cairo, in this North African country.

definitions.meaning: a court's finding that someone committed the crime

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a strongly held view and the formal finding of guilt by a court.

indicators.note: changes made to says the letters of the building's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cosmetic alterations have been carried out on the Washington legislature building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes made to' rearranges CAPITOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to sight or the eye is what visual means, a near synonym.

clue.text: Revolutionary's son to join staff and figure on the board

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary, with the possessive S kept
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies
to staff is to man, provide workers for

explanation.surface: A rebel leader's boy signs up as an employee and becomes a director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure on the board' looks like a company director but means a game piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A king, rook or pawn is a piece, a figure standing on the chequered board.

clue.text: He deprives others of their occupation

definitions.text: He deprives others of their occupation

parts.words: He deprives others of their occupation
parts.note: occupation means living in a place, not a job: someone who turns tenants out

explanation.walkthrough: 'occupation' suggests a job, as if someone sacks workers; here it is occupancy of a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord or bailiff who removes tenants from a property ends their occupancy.

clue.text: Feel feathers should be used in landing

parts.note: to touch is to feel
down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: Advice that feather cushions be used to soften an arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: When an aircraft lands, the wheels meeting the runway is its arrival on the ground.

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something gives a modest boost to the attention customers receive.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening prayer in church, held in the late day, is a religious service.

parts.note: sub is Latin for under, as in subway
the lime and the linden are the same tree

explanation.surface: Praise for a performance of a song titled after a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted song title is a distraction: its two words simply give the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Of awe-inspiring excellence or beauty, exalted; a close synonym for magnificent.

clue.text: Large number make certain you get blame

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to ensure is to make certain

explanation.surface: Many people guarantee that you will be held responsible.
explanation.definitionFit: To criticise formally or reprove is a synonym for finding fault.

clue.text: Crown taking firm course with uprising

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: tenor means general course or drift, as in the tenor of a conversation

explanation.surface: A royal headdress joins a company that follows a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns TENOR into RONET.
explanation.definitionFit: A small crown worn by nobles below sovereign rank is a lesser crown.

definitions.meaning: a group of students taught together

explanation.definitionFit: As an informal adjective it means excellent; as a noun it is a group of schoolchildren.

clue.text: A newly married woman has no right to stay

indicators.note: has no says a letter is dropped from the word for the woman

parts.note: a bride is a woman just married

explanation.surface: A newlywed is told she has no legal right to remain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' removes R from BRIDE to leave BIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain or dwell somewhere is an old sense of the verb, as in abide with me.

clue.text: Electoral divisions, locally, or in branches

indicators.note: in says the short word sits inside the word for branches

parts.note: boughs are branches of a tree

explanation.surface: Constituencies, in local speech, or in tree branches; a deliberately odd pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: Towns with their own councils and parliamentary seats are local units of government.

clue.text: He introduces you and me with that woman

parts.note: us is the pronoun for you and me
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A man presents a couple to a female acquaintance.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant at a ceremony or court who shows people in and announces them introduces guests.

parts.note: a banker in crosswords is a river, something with banks; here the river flowing through Oxford

explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' suggests a financier; it is something that has banks, a river. The Thames at Oxford is known by its own local name.
explanation.definitionFit: The stretch of the Thames flowing through Oxford goes by this local name.

definitions.meaning: fake, copied, as in faux leather
from the saying that copying is the sincerest form of flattery

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means fake or copied; as a noun it is copying, called the sincerest flattery.

parts.note: eye-catching means literally catching an eye, the loop of a fastener on clothes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye-catching' suggests striking; it means devices that catch eyes, as in fastenings of the type called hooks and eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Curved metal catches on garments engage small loops called eyes to fasten them.

indicators.note: awkward says the letters of ones are put in an ungainly new order

explanation.surface: Difficult people keep voting against everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' reorders ONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Votes against a motion in parliament are counted as the nays.

indicators.note: mixed says the letters of the two words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Nine boxes of assorted fruit arrive at a market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges NINE CRATES.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned variety of peach is a stone fruit.
